case_name: Sushila Chemicals Private Limited and another v Bharat Coking Coal Limited and others
petitioner: Sushila Chemicals Private Limited and another
facts: Pursuant to public advertisements issued by Coal India Limited calling upon entrepreneurs to establish coal based industries, the appellants purchased technology and established plants for manufacturing special smokeless fuel during 1990-1991.
The appellants continued to run their respective plants and manufacture special smokeless fuel by processing the coal supplied by BCCL to them.

On 18.10.2007, the Government of India, Ministry of Coal discontinued the traditional linkage system and adopted a new coal distribution policy under which coal was to be supplied to different consumers through a Fuel Supply Agreement (FSA) at notified prices.
issues: Whether the suspension of supply of coal by BCCL to the appellants was reasonable and arbitrary
Whether the Division Bench of the Patna High Court correctly held that resumption of supply of coal could not be ordered in larger public interest
petitioner_arguments: The plants of the appellants were manufacturing smokeless fuel and the object of the FSA executed by BCCL was to provide coal for the plants
Suspension of supplies of coal by BCCL without terminating the agreement (FSA) is unreasonable and arbitrary and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution
The FIR lodged by the CBI did not have sufficient materials in its possession, making the suspension of supplies of coal to the appellants arbitrary and unreasonable
respondent_arguments: The FIR lodged by a premier investigating agency like the CBI and the chequered history of the appellants before the FIR were sufficient for BCCL to suspend the supply of coal to the appellants
Investigation into the allegations made in the FIR has already been completed by the CBI and charge sheet has been filed against the appellants
court_reasoning: The Division Bench of the Patna High Court placed reliance on a judgment of the Division Bench of the Patna High Court dated 05.07.2002 passed in M/s. Central Coal Field Limited vs. M/s, Aman Lime Works (LPA No.701 of 2002) and held that resumption of supply of coal cannot be directed by the court so long as the respondents do not consider the explanation of the appellants
The learned Single Judge had quashed the order directing suspension of supplies of coal to the appellants and allowed the writ petitions
holding: The appeals were allowed, but the appellants were directed to take a final decision pursuant to the show cause notice dated 16.07.2009 at an early date
The respondents were directed to resume supply of coal to the appellants
